'''Cade Brem McNown''' (born January 12, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for four seasons. He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]], winning the [[Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award]], the [[Pop Warner Trophy]], and [[Pac-12 Offensive Player of the Year|Pac 10 Co-Offensive Player of the Year]] in 1998. McNown was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the first round of the [[1999 NFL draft]], but his tenure would only last two seasons due to injuries and inconsistent play. He spent his final two seasons as a backup for the [[Miami Dolphins]] and [[San Francisco 49ers]]. McNown was inducted to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2020.

'''Caesar Edward Belser''' (September 13, 1944 – March 5, 2016) was an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]] and [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] who played in the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He is the father of [[Jason Belser]].

He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff|Arkansas AM&N]], and professionally in the AFL and the NFL for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and later the [[San Francisco 49ers]].

Belser died on the weekend of March 5, 2016, according to his family. He was 71. He was battling lung cancer, as well as neurological damage from playing football. Per his family's wishes, his brain will be donated to scientific research.<ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article64662352.html Former Chiefs safety Caesar Belser dies, will have brain donated to science]</ref>
